text: A stale feed degrades Velocity in steps. The AMM stops quoting first, while orderbook matching, margin and liquidation continue. Once the feed is stale for margin, margin-gated actions revert, including opening a position and withdrawing collateral while holding liabilities, even on markets the account does not trade. Liquidations and trigger orders still run, so a stale price does not protect an underwater account. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

text: A Drift/Velocity market with no listed feed can use a prelaunch oracle that is self-referential: its price is the market's own mark TWAP, capped at an admin-set max_price, and its confidence is the larger of the ask/bid TWAP spread and the mark standard deviation (PrelaunchOracle::update). Velocity says such markets sit in the tiers with no insurance coverage and the widest confidence tolerance because they have no outside anchor. (medium confidence)

text: Two divergence checks run against the 5-minute oracle TWAP. The 10% band (AMM mark or live oracle against the TWAP, whichever is further) reverts with PriceBandsBreached and blocks P&L settlement, perp P&L deficit resolution and the P&L pool fee sweep. The 50% band (live oracle against the TWAP) skips fills, reverts post-fill checks, reverts stop and take-profit triggers, and reverts all four liquidation paths. The docs state that during a genuine dislocation a position can be neither closed by its owner nor liquidated until the price returns inside the band. This qualifies the oracles page's 'liquidation still runs'. Program defaults are 10% and 50%. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
keywords: Pyth and Switchboard oracle use in perp pricing

text: One new oracle sample can move a market's running oracle TWAP by at most a per-tier band: 10% for tier A, 20% for B, 50% for C and about 33% for Speculative, Highly Speculative and Isolated. The bands are not monotonic, because tier C is wider than the tail tiers. A large genuine move therefore takes several intervals to enter the TWAP, and the divergence bands stay tight meanwhile. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
keywords: Pyth and Switchboard oracle use in perp pricing

text: Each action accepts a different subset of grades (Drift Rust is_oracle_valid_for_action; Velocity docs table). Auction-skipping AMM fills need Valid; low-risk AMM fills also accept stale-for-AMM within the low-risk threshold; margin calculation rejects non-positive, too volatile, too uncertain and stale-for-margin; liquidation and trigger orders reject only non-positive and too volatile; TWAP and AMM-curve updates reject only non-positive; funding updates and PnL settlement accept Valid, stale-for-AMM, insufficient-data-points and stale-for-margin. text: Jupiter Perps aggregates prices from three onchain oracles: Edge by Chaos Labs (primary), and Chainlink and Pyth (verification and fallback). If Edge is not stale and within a threshold of both Chainlink and Pyth, the Edge price is used. If Edge is stale or outside the threshold, Chainlink and Pyth are compared and, if within the threshold of each other, the more recent is used. If two or more oracles fail, no price update occurs. Updates happen during trade execution and via an independent keeper. The Beta (orderbook) markets run on a separate engine, and their stock-market prices come from Chainlink. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

text: Jupiter Perps separates trade commitment from execution. The app picks per action between request-and-fulfillment (the trader submits a request transaction, a keeper validates it and submits a second execution transaction; limit and TP/SL orders execute this way) and a single transaction co-signed by a Jupiter keeper (closing from jup.ag by default). On the request path the trade is not live until the keeper's fulfillment confirms. Pyth's best practices recommend the same separation (delayed settlement or commit-reveal) so the protocol can observe price changes before it fills. (medium confidence)

text: A perpetual has no expiry or delivery, so nothing in the contract forces its price to track the underlying. Funding and margin both need a reference price the exchange does not produce. Velocity's docs add that the exchange's own last price is the one number a trader can move, so each market carries an oracle account, written by someone other than the trader, that holds a price, a confidence interval and a timestamp. Margin, liquidation, funding and the AMM quote are all measured against it. Pyth's perps use-case page says oracle prices enter the funding-rate calculation and that the mark price (built from spot or index prices) drives PnL and liquidation. (high confidence)
